title: A low-mass TOI-682 fit retains bounded 7:3 angle motion through 10,000-year Newtonian and precession tests
abstract: We test the unresolved critical-angle motion of a published low-mass TOI-682 timing fit. In 10,000-year Newtonian and relativistic-precession-potential integrations, one 7:3 angle stays within ranges of 1.05089 and 1.05435 turns. Its net changes are -0.09619 and -0.18862 turns, while the periapse difference makes 7.80 and 7.93 turns. Thus the near-zero net rotation in a prior 1,000-year test persists as bounded, modulated motion. A full range just above one turn does not imply cumulative circulation. Six initial outer-period perturbations up to 0.001 days retain this structure in 3,000-year Newtonian tests. The high-mass control instead has bounded periapse difference and more than 4,445 turns in all five critical angles. These are finite tests of selected fitted states, not a resonance detection, a posterior probability, a new timing fit or a formation history. The precession potential is an approximate sensitivity test and is not a full relativistic data fit. We preserve input hashes, code, simulated tracks, checks and static figures.

display.caption: Two published timing fits retain distinct critical-angle and periapse histories in two 10,000-year force tests.
The low-mass state has a bounded, modulated angle while its outer eccentricity changes.
